source.title: Gad Elmaleh – Les petits mensonges du quotidien (Montreux Comedy Festival 2023)
source.timestamp_precision: caption-block start from the transcript; refine +/-3s on footage

candidates.context: He's 50, scrolls Instagram, and sees half-naked girls quoting philosophers. One poses next to a private jet with a Vuitton bag and writes « Merci, la vie. »
candidates.punchline: « La vie… C'est la vie qui a payé tout ça, oui ! Jean-Jacques Lavie, 78 ans. »
candidates.why_funny: Wordplay misdirection: 'la vie' (life) turns into a sugar daddy's surname, and the specific age makes the picture land. The tag (he can't even move on the plane) extends it.
candidates.meme_idea: Mock Instagram post (original graphic) for « Merci, la vie. »; freeze + impact on « Jean-Jacques Lavie »; editorial caption « Merci qui ? »

source.title: Gad Elmaleh – Les petits mensonges du quotidien (Montreux Comedy Festival 2023)
source.timestamp_precision: caption-block start from the transcript; refine +/-3s on footage

candidates.context: On a train, the woman next to him texts « Devine à côté de qui je suis assise : Gad Elmaleh » (misspelled) and her friend replies « Naaaan ! ». He reads it all over her shoulder.
candidates.punchline: Ten minutes later: « Oh, mais vous n'êtes pas… ? » — « T'es sérieuse ? J'ai les preuves. J'ai le ‹ Naaaan › ! »
candidates.why_funny: Dramatic irony: the audience saw the texts with him, so her fake 'aren't you…?' is a lie we can prove. Plus the act-out of 'Naaaan'.
candidates.meme_idea: Animated chat bubbles recreating the texts he quotes (original graphic); 'WAIT… WHAT?!' sticker on her question.

source.title: Gad Elmaleh – Les petits mensonges du quotidien (Montreux Comedy Festival 2023)
source.timestamp_precision: caption-block start from the transcript; refine +/-3s on footage

candidates.context: Dating much younger women: at a restaurant he asks if she likes it, and she answers « J'avoue. »
candidates.punchline: « J'ai attendu qu'elle avoue un truc toute la soirée… ‹ Askip ›, je vois de la lessive. Arrête ! »
candidates.why_funny: A 50-year-old taking youth slang literally ('j'avoue' = I confess; 'askip' sounds like a detergent ad). Two quick hits, very shareable across generations.
candidates.meme_idea: Slang 'dictionary card' overlay (j'avoue = carrément, askip = à ce qu'il paraît); boing on « lessive ».

candidates.context: In Morocco, a woman comes up to him at the hotel: « Gad, dommage que vous soyez marié. » He says: « Ben moi, je ne suis pas marié. »
candidates.punchline: « Elle me dit : ‹ Ah ! Moi oui. › »
candidates.why_funny: A clean three-line reversal; the pause before « Moi oui » is the joke. An ideal 15–20s one-liner.
candidates.meme_idea: Crickets SFX + 'AWKWARD.' sticker after the reveal; caption « Elle avait un plan ».

source.title: Gad Elmaleh – Les petits mensonges du quotidien (Montreux Comedy Festival 2023)
source.timestamp_precision: caption-block start from the transcript; refine +/-3s on footage

candidates.context: He wants Sophie Marceau's name tattooed. The advice he gets: do your first tattoo somewhere you don't care about.
candidates.punchline: « Du coup, je vais le faire… à Annemasse. »
candidates.why_funny: The body-part expectation flips into a place name. It lands hardest with a Swiss/Geneva audience (Annemasse is a French border town), and it needs the Marceau setup.
candidates.meme_idea: Map-pin graphic on Annemasse for viewers who aren't local.

candidates.context: He explains the encore ritual: everyone pretends. The comedian hides, and the crowd pretends to want him back.
candidates.punchline: « Finished my show, walked off the stage. I came back, they were gone. »

candidates.meme_idea: Freeze on his face + crickets; caption 'New York doesn't do encores'.
